text: Git branching is a core part of any version control workflow. Instead of working directly on the main code, developers create feature branches to build new functions or fix bugs in isolation. This keeps the main branch stable and ready for release. Once the work on a feature branch is complete, the developer submits a pull request. This acts as a formal request to review and discuss the changes before merging them into the main branch. After a successful review and testing, the branch is merged. This process encourages collaboration, prevents conflicts, and makes it easy to track exactly when and how each change was added.
